where: Section 2, end of the undecidable-for-CFG paragraph
problem: The text lists only three undecidable questions for context-free grammars (is L(G) = Σ*, are two CFGs equivalent, is G ambiguous) but then says "for a DFA all four of these are decidable". The count contradicts the list, and no fourth question exists, so a student counting the items gets confused about what was claimed.
fix: Change the count to match the list: "Notice that for a DFA the corresponding questions (universality and equivalence of two machines) are decidable; the jump to a machine with unbounded memory is what destroys the algorithm."

problem: P_TM = {⟨M⟩ : M ever writes a stated symbol a on its tape} leaves the starting tape and the status of a undefined. If a already sits on the input tape the answer is trivially yes, and the undecidability claim only holds when the machine starts on a blank tape and a is a fixed non-blank tape symbol. As written a student may read the problem as decidable.
fix: P_TM = {⟨M⟩ : M, started on a blank tape, at some point writes the fixed non-blank tape symbol a}. This is undecidable: from ⟨M,w⟩ build M′ that simulates M on w and writes a only on acceptance.
